title: Forces and Equilibrium Module 2 Lesson 1: Three-Force Equilibrium Unknown Force Angle custom practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, numerical values and physical configurations are original; mapped Cambridge past-paper evidence informs cognitive demand and assessment structure only.

parts.prompt: A particle is in equilibrium under the action of three coplanar forces: a force of $12\text{ N}$ along the positive $x$-axis, a force of $16\text{ N}$ along the positive $y$-axis, and a third force $\mathbf{F}$. Calculate the magnitude of $\mathbf{F}$, and find the angle that $\mathbf{F}$ makes below the negative $x$-axis, giving your answer correct to 1 decimal place.

Three coplanar forces hold a particle in equilibrium: a horizontal force of $30\text{ N}$ along the positive $x$-axis, a force of $40\text{ N}$ at an angle of $60^\circ$ above the positive $x$-axis, and a third force $\mathbf{P}$ acting at an angle $\theta$ below the negative $x$-axis. Calculate the horizontal and vertical components of $\mathbf{P}$, and hence determine the magnitude $P$ correct to 3 significant figures.

A particle of mass $3\text{ kg}$ is suspended in equilibrium by a light inextensible string inclined at an angle $\theta$ to the vertical and held displaced by a horizontal force of $15\text{ N}$. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, calculate the tension $T$ in the string, and find the angle $\theta$ correct to 1 decimal place.

Three forces of magnitudes $8\text{ N}$, $15\text{ N}$, and $17\text{ N}$ act at a point and maintain the particle in equilibrium. By considering the triangle of forces, deduce the angle between the lines of action of the $8\text{ N}$ force and the $15\text{ N}$ force.

A particle is held in equilibrium by three coplanar forces: a horizontal force of $24\text{ N}$ in the positive $x$-direction, a downward vertical force of $18\text{ N}$ in the negative $y$-direction, and a force of magnitude $P$ acting at an angle $\theta$ above the negative $x$-axis. Calculate the value of $P$, and find the angle $\theta$ correct to 1 decimal place.

Three coplanar forces of magnitudes $10\text{ N}$, $T$, and $W$ hold a particle in equilibrium. The angle between the $10\text{ N}$ force and force $T$ is $120^\circ$, and the angle between force $T$ and force $W$ is $90^\circ$. Find the angle between the $10\text{ N}$ force and force $W$, and calculate the value of $T$.

questions.prompt: A particle of weight $W = 48\text{ N}$ is suspended from a fixed support by a light inextensible string. A horizontal force of magnitude $F$ is applied to the particle such that the string is taut and inclined at an angle $\alpha$ to the vertical, where $\cos\alpha = \frac{12}{13}$ and $\sin\alpha = \frac{5}{13}$. The particle is held in equilibrium.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: By resolving forces vertically in equilibrium, calculate the tension $T$ in the string.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: By resolving forces horizontally, determine the magnitude of the horizontal force $F$, and calculate the angle $\alpha$ correct to 1 decimal place.

questions.prompt:
Three coplanar forces act on a particle in equilibrium:
- A horizontal force of magnitude $36\text{ N}$ in the positive $x$-direction.
- A vertical force of magnitude $27\text{ N}$ in the negative $y$-direction.
- A force of magnitude $P$ acting at an angle $\theta$ above the negative $x$-axis.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Write down the equations for horizontal and vertical equilibrium, expressing $P\cos\theta$ and $P\sin\theta$ in terms of the given forces.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the exact value of $P$, and calculate the angle $\theta$ correct to 1 decimal place.

questions.prompt:
Three coplanar forces act at a point $O$ and maintain a particle in equilibrium:
- Force $\mathbf{F}_1$ has magnitude $50\text{ N}$ and acts at an angle of $40^\circ$ above the positive $x$-axis.
- Force $\mathbf{F}_2$ has magnitude $35\text{ N}$ and acts along the positive $y$-axis.
- Force $\mathbf{F}_3$ has unknown magnitude $P$ and acts at an angle $\theta$ below the negative $x$-axis ($0^\circ < \theta < 90^\circ$).

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: By resolving horizontally and vertically in equilibrium, calculate the value of $P\cos\theta$ and the value of $P\sin\theta$, giving each value correct to 3 decimal places.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Hence find the value of $\theta$ correct to 1 decimal place, and determine the magnitude $P$ correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.prompt: A small smooth ring $R$ of mass $0.8\text{ kg}$ is threaded on a light inextensible string whose ends are attached to two fixed points $A$ and $B$ on the same horizontal ceiling. A horizontal force of magnitude $X$ pulls the ring such that segment $AR$ makes an angle of $30^\circ$ with the vertical and segment $BR$ makes an angle of $60^\circ$ with the vertical. The ring is held in equilibrium. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Explain why the tension $T$ is uniform throughout the string, and by resolving vertically in equilibrium, calculate the exact value of $T$ in surd form.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: By resolving horizontally in equilibrium, determine the exact value of the horizontal force $X$ in surd form, and give its value correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.prompt: A particle of mass $m = 2.5\text{ kg}$ is held in equilibrium on a smooth inclined plane making an angle of $30^\circ$ with the horizontal by a force of magnitude $P$ acting at an angle $\theta$ above the line of greatest slope of the plane. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: By resolving forces parallel to the inclined plane, express $P\cos\theta$ in terms of the component of weight.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Given that $P = 15\text{ N}$, calculate the angle $\theta$ correct to 1 decimal place.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: By resolving forces perpendicular to the inclined plane, calculate the normal reaction $R_N$ exerted by the plane on the particle correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.prompt: A particle $P$ of weight $W = 60\text{ N}$ is suspended in equilibrium from two light inextensible strings $AP$ and $BP$ attached to fixed points $A$ and $B$ on a horizontal ceiling. The lengths of the strings are $AP = 0.6\text{ m}$ and $BP = 0.8\text{ m}$, and the distance between the support points $A$ and $B$ is $1.0\text{ m}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Show that $\triangle APB$ is a right-angled triangle, and determine the angle $\alpha$ that string $AP$ makes with the horizontal ceiling and the angle $\beta$ that string $BP$ makes with the horizontal ceiling.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: By resolving forces along the directions of the two perpendicular strings, or by resolving horizontally and vertically, calculate the tension $T_A$ in string $AP$ and the tension $T_B$ in string $BP$.

questions.prompt: A particle of weight $W = 80\text{ N}$ is suspended by a light inextensible string inclined at an angle of $60^\circ$ to the vertical. A force $\mathbf{P}$ of magnitude $P$ is applied to the particle at an angle $\theta$ above the horizontal ($0^\circ \leqslant \theta \leqslant 90^\circ$). The particle is held in equilibrium.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt:
By resolving forces perpendicular to the string, show that:
$$P\cos(\theta - 30^\circ) = 40\sqrt{3}$$
and explain why the string tension $T$ does not appear in this equation.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Deduce the minimum possible magnitude of $P$ and the corresponding value of $\theta$, and calculate the tension $T$ in the string when $P$ takes this minimum value.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Suppose instead that the applied force is horizontal (so that $\theta = 0^\circ$). Calculate the new magnitude of $P$ and the new tension $T$ in the string required to maintain equilibrium.
